cohort: The study included 567 postpartum women aged 15-44 years from six health facilities in the Njombe region, Tanzania.
finding: The study found a Caesarean section prevalence of 45.5% in Njombe, significantly exceeding national and global averages, and identified several demographic and clinical factors associated with this high rate.
mod_finding: Factors associated with a higher likelihood of Caesarean section delivery included being single, late first ANC visit, maternal height <= 150 cm, birth weight > 4.1 kg, gestational age >= 43 weeks, and referral from health centers.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from post-delivery women.
